annotations.title: Get every planet's position on a date

description:
Returns where every body is at an instant, WITH NO BIRTH DATA AND NO PLACE REQUIRED: Sun, Moon, the eight planets and the two lunar nodes, each with geocentric ecliptic longitude, sign and degree in BOTH the tropical (Western) and sidereal (Vedic) zodiacs, ecliptic latitude, longitude speed, retrograde state and distance. It covers "what sign is Venus in", "where is Mercury right now", "what sign is the Moon in today", "when did Mars enter Gemini": any position question about the sky with no particular person's chart in it.

NO PLACE IS NEEDED: a geocentric longitude is identical for every observer on Earth, so a sky question needs no birthplace and no chart. An observer's lat and lon are used only for rise and set times.

Planetary positions are what a model half-remembers from training tables: shape right, date wrong, stated with confidence. A planet sits within a degree of a cusp for days, so "Venus is in Scorpio" can be true on Tuesday and false on Wednesday; the Moon moves half a degree an hour and changes sign roughly every 2.3 days, so its row depends on the hour as well as the date.

BOTH ZODIACS COME BACK IN EVERY ROW: a Western reader wants result.bodies[].sign, a Vedic reader result.bodies[].siderealSign, and they differ by result.ayanamsa, about 24 degrees, very nearly a whole sign, so the two are usually DIFFERENT SIGNS. Rahu and Ketu are the MEAN nodes (result.nodeNote). A retrograde period's start and end come from check_retrogrades.

Results include an attribution line and a permalink.

date.description: The date, ISO YYYY-MM-DD, 1700-2200. Example: "2026-09-21". Omit: today (UTC).

lat.description: Observer latitude in decimal degrees as a string. Example: "64.1466". Send with lon. Rise and set only.

lon.description: Observer longitude in decimal degrees as a string. Example: "-21.9426". Send with lat. Rise and set only.

place.description: Observer town or city. Example: "Reykjavik, Iceland". OPTIONAL: it changes no position, only rise and set times.

time.description: Time of day HH:MM in UTC, not local and not a birth time. Example: "12:00". Matters for the Moon, which moves about half a degree an hour.

tz.description: IANA zone or numeric UTC offset hours for the local rise and set times. Example: "Atlantic/Reykjavik".

name: get_planetary_positions
title: Get every planet's position on a date
